items.text:
यस्य चितं द्रवीभूतं कृपया सर्वजन्तुषु ।
तस्य ज्ञानेन मोक्षेण किं जटाभस्मलेपनैः ॥ १ ॥
items.tr:
yasya citaṃ dravībhūtaṃ kṛpayā sarvajantuṣu |
tasya jñānena mokṣeṇa kiṃ jaṭābhasmalepanaiḥ || 1 ||
items.en: One whose heart melts with compassion for all living beings has no need of knowledge, of freedom, of matted hair or of smearing ash on the body.

items.text:
एकमेवाक्षरं यस्तु गुरुः शिष्यं प्रबोधयेत् ।
पृथिव्यां नास्ति तद्द्रव्यं यद् दत्त्वा चानृणी भवेत् ॥ २ ॥
items.tr:
ekamevākṣaraṃ yastu guruḥ śiṣyaṃ prabodhayet |
pṛthivyāṃ nāsti taddravyaṃ yad dattvā cānṛṇī bhavet || 2 ||
items.en: If a teacher teaches a pupil even one single letter, there is no wealth on earth that the pupil could give to repay that debt.

items.text:
खलानां कण्टकानां च द्विविधैव प्रतिक्रिया ।
उपानद् मुखभङ्गो वा दूरतैव विसर्जनम् ॥ ३ ॥
items.tr:
khalānāṃ kaṇṭakānāṃ ca dvividhaiva pratikriyā |
upānad mukhabhaṅgo vā dūrataiva visarjanam || 3 ||
items.en: For wicked people and for thorns there are only two remedies: crush them with a shoe, or keep far away from them.

items.text:
कुचैलिनं दन्तमलोपधारिणां
बह्वाशिनंनिष्ठुरभाषिणां च ।
सूर्योदये वाऽस्तमिते शयानं
विमुञ्चति श्रीर्यदि चक्रपाणिः ॥ ४ ॥
items.tr:
kucailinaṃ dantamalopadhāriṇāṃ
bahvāśinaṃniṣṭhurabhāṣiṇāṃ ca |
sūryodaye vā'stamite śayānaṃ
vimuñcati śrīryadi cakrapāṇiḥ || 4 ||
items.en: Good fortune leaves a person who wears dirty clothes, has unclean teeth, eats too much, speaks harshly, and sleeps at sunrise or sunset, even if he were Vishnu himself.

items.text:
त्यजन्ति मित्राणि धनैर्विहीनं
दाराश्च भृत्याश्च सुहृज्जनाश्च ।
तं चार्थवन्तं पुनराश्रयन्ते ।
ह्यर्थो हि लोके पुरुषस्य बन्धुः ॥ ५ ॥
items.tr:
tyajanti mitrāṇi dhanairvihīnaṃ
dārāśca bhṛtyāśca suhṛjjanāśca |
taṃ cārthavantaṃ punarāśrayante |
hyartho hi loke puruṣasya bandhuḥ || 5 ||
items.en: When a man loses his money, his friends, wife, servants and well-wishers leave him; when he is rich again, they come back. In this world, money is a man's true relative.

items.text:
अन्यायोपार्जितं द्रव्यं दश वर्षाणि तिष्ठति ।
प्राप्ते एकादशे वर्षे समूलं च विनश्यति ॥ ६ ॥
items.tr:
anyāyopārjitaṃ dravyaṃ daśa varṣāṇi tiṣṭhati |
prāpte ekādaśe varṣe samūlaṃ ca vinaśyati || 6 ||
items.en: Wealth gained unjustly stays for ten years; when the eleventh year comes, it is lost along with its roots.

items.text:
अयुक्तं स्वामिनो युक्तं युक्तं नीचस्य दूषणम् ।
अमृतं राहवे मृत्युर्विषं शंकरभूषणम् ॥ ७ ॥
items.tr:
ayuktaṃ svāmino yuktaṃ yuktaṃ nīcasya dūṣaṇam |
amṛtaṃ rāhave mṛtyurviṣaṃ śaṃkarabhūṣaṇam || 7 ||
items.en: What is wrong in a great person passes as right, and what is right in a low person is called a fault: nectar brought death to Rahu, while poison became an ornament for Shiva.

items.text:
तद्भोजनं यद् द्विजभुक्तशेषं
तत्सौहृदं यत्क्रियते परस्मिन् ।
सा प्राज्ञता या न करोति पापं
दम्भं विना यः क्रियते पापं
दम्भं विना यः क्रियते स धर्मः ॥ ८ ॥
items.tr:
tadbhojanaṃ yad dvijabhuktaśeṣaṃ
tatsauhṛdaṃ yatkriyate parasmin |
sā prājñatā yā na karoti pāpaṃ
dambhaṃ vinā yaḥ kriyate pāpaṃ
dambhaṃ vinā yaḥ kriyate sa dharmaḥ || 8 ||
items.en: True food is what is left after the learned have eaten; true friendship is that shown to others; true wisdom is that which does no wrong; and true righteousness is that done without show.

items.text:
मणिर्लुण्ठति पादाग्रे काचः शिरसि धार्यते ।
क्रय विक्रयवेलायां काचः काचो मणिर्मणिः ॥ ९ ॥
items.tr:
maṇirluṇṭhati pādāgre kācaḥ śirasi dhāryate |
kraya vikrayavelāyāṃ kācaḥ kāco maṇirmaṇiḥ || 9 ||
items.en: A jewel may lie rolling at one's feet and glass may be worn on the head, but when it is time to buy and sell, glass is glass and a jewel is a jewel.

items.text:
अनन्तंशास्त्रं बहुलाश्च विद्याः
अल्पं च कालो बहुविघ्नता च ।
यत्सारभूतं तदुपासनीयं,
हंसो यथा क्षीरमिवम्बुमध्यात् ॥ १० ॥
items.tr:
anantaṃśāstraṃ bahulāśca vidyāḥ
alpaṃ ca kālo bahuvighnatā ca |
yatsārabhūtaṃ tadupāsanīyaṃ,
haṃso yathā kṣīramivambumadhyāt || 10 ||
items.en: The scriptures are endless and there are many branches of learning, but time is short and obstacles are many; so take only the essence, as a swan takes the milk out of water.

items.text:
दूरागतं पथि श्रान्तं वृथा च गृहमागतम् ।
अनर्चयित्वा यो भुङ्क्ते स वै चाण्डाल उच्यते ॥ ११ ॥
items.tr:
dūrāgataṃ pathi śrāntaṃ vṛthā ca gṛhamāgatam |
anarcayitvā yo bhuṅkte sa vai cāṇḍāla ucyate || 11 ||
items.en: One who eats without first honouring a guest who has come from far away, tired from the road, and arrived unexpectedly at his home is called an outcast.

items.text:
पठन्ति चतुरो वेदान् धर्मशास्त्राण्यनेकशः ।
आत्मानं नैव जानन्ति दवी पाकरसं यथा ॥ १२ ॥
items.tr:
paṭhanti caturo vedān dharmaśāstrāṇyanekaśaḥ |
ātmānaṃ naiva jānanti davī pākarasaṃ yathā || 12 ||
items.en: Some read the four Vedas and many books of law, yet they do not know their own self, just as a ladle does not know the taste of the food it stirs.

items.text:
धन्या द्विजमयि नौका विपरीता भवार्णवे ।
तरन्त्यधोगताः सर्वे उपरिस्थाः पतन्त्यधः ॥ १३ ॥
items.tr:
dhanyā dvijamayi naukā viparītā bhavārṇave |
tarantyadhogatāḥ sarve uparisthāḥ patantyadhaḥ || 13 ||
items.en: Blessed is the boat of the twice-born, which works the other way round on the sea of worldly life: all who stay low cross over, and those who stay on top sink.

items.text:
अयममृतनिधानं नायकोऽप्यौषधीनां ।
अमृतमयशरीरः कान्तियुक्तोऽपि चन्द्रः ॥
भवति विगतरश्मिर्मण्डलं प्राप्य भानोः ।
परसदननिविष्टः को लघुत्वं न याति ॥ १४ ॥
items.tr:
ayamamṛtanidhānaṃ nāyako'pyauṣadhīnāṃ |
amṛtamayaśarīraḥ kāntiyukto'pi candraḥ ||
bhavati vigataraśmirmaṇḍalaṃ prāpya bhānoḥ |
parasadananiviṣṭaḥ ko laghutvaṃ na yāti || 14 ||
items.en: The moon is a store of nectar, lord of healing plants, with a body made of nectar and full of light; yet it loses its rays when it enters the sun's circle. Who does not become small when living in another's house?

items.text:
अलिरयं नलिनीदलमध्यगः
कमलिनीमकरन्दमदालसः ।
विधिवशात्परदेशमुपागतः
कुटजपुष्परसं बहु मन्यते ॥ १५ ॥
items.tr:
alirayaṃ nalinīdalamadhyagaḥ
kamalinīmakarandamadālasaḥ |
vidhivaśātparadeśamupāgataḥ
kuṭajapuṣparasaṃ bahu manyate || 15 ||
items.en: This bee, which once lived among lotus petals, lazy and drunk on lotus nectar, now finds itself by fate in a strange land and thinks highly of the juice of the kutaja flower.

items.text:
पीतः क्रुध्देन तातश्चरणतलहता वल्लभो येन रोषा-
दाबाल्याद्विप्रवर्यैः स्ववदनविवरे धार्यते वैरिणी में ।
गेहं मे छेदयन्ति प्रतिदिवसमुमाकान्तपूजानिमित्तं
तस्मात्खिन्नासदात्हंद्विजकुलनिलयं नाथ युक्तं त्यजामि ॥ १६ ॥
items.tr:
pītaḥ krudhdena tātaścaraṇatalahatā vallabho yena roṣā-
dābālyādvipravaryaiḥ svavadanavivare dhāryate vairiṇī meṃ |
gehaṃ me chedayanti pratidivasamumākāntapūjānimittaṃ
tasmātkhinnāsadāthaṃdvijakulanilayaṃ nātha yuktaṃ tyajāmi || 16 ||
items.en: (Lakshmi speaks:) One Brahmin in anger drank up my father, the ocean; another kicked my beloved in rage; from childhood the best Brahmins keep my rival, learning, in their mouths; and every day they cut my home, the lotus, to worship Shiva. So, my Lord, I am always unhappy and stay away from the homes of Brahmins.

items.text:
बंधनानि खलु सन्ति बहूनि प्रेमरज्जुकृतबन्धनमन्यत् ।
दारुभेदनिपुणोऽपिषण्डघ्निर्निष्क्रियोभवति पंकजकोशे ॥ १७ ॥
items.tr:
baṃdhanāni khalu santi bahūni premarajjukṛtabandhanamanyat |
dārubhedanipuṇo'piṣaṇḍaghnirniṣkriyobhavati paṃkajakośe || 17 ||
items.en: There are many kinds of bonds, but the bond made by the rope of love is different: the bee, skilled at boring through wood, becomes helpless inside the closed lotus bud.

items.text:
छिन्नोऽपि चंदनतरुर्न जहाति गन्धं
वृध्दोऽपि वारणपतिर्न जहाति लीलाम् ।
यंत्रार्पितो मधुरतां न जहाति चेक्षुः
क्षीणोऽपि न त्यजति शीलगुणान् कुलीनः ॥ १८ ॥
items.tr:
chinno'pi caṃdanatarurna jahāti gandhaṃ
vṛdhdo'pi vāraṇapatirna jahāti līlām |
yaṃtrārpito madhuratāṃ na jahāti cekṣuḥ
kṣīṇo'pi na tyajati śīlaguṇān kulīnaḥ || 18 ||
items.en: Even when cut, the sandalwood tree does not lose its scent; even when old, the king of elephants does not lose his playfulness; even when pressed in the mill, sugarcane does not lose its sweetness; and even when poor, a person of good family does not give up good character.

items.text:
उर्व्यां कोऽपि महीधरो लघुतरो दोर्भ्यां धृतो लीलया
तेन त्वांदिवि भूतले च ससतं गोवर्धनी गीयसे ।
त्वां त्रैलोक्यधरं वहामि कुचयोरग्रेण तद् गण्यते
किंवा केशव भाषणेन बहुनापुण्यैर्यशो लभ्यते ॥ १९ ॥
items.tr:
urvyāṃ ko'pi mahīdharo laghutaro dorbhyāṃ dhṛto līlayā
tena tvāṃdivi bhūtale ca sasataṃ govardhanī gīyase |
tvāṃ trailokyadharaṃ vahāmi kucayoragreṇa tad gaṇyate
kiṃvā keśava bhāṣaṇena bahunāpuṇyairyaśo labhyate || 19 ||
items.en: (Radha says to Krishna:) You playfully lifted some small mountain from the earth with your arms, and so in heaven and on earth you are always praised as the holder of Govardhana. I carry you, the holder of the three worlds, on my breast, yet no one counts that. Keshava, what is the use of more talk? Fame comes through good fortune.
